tidyagsim

tidyagsim extends AlphaSimR with the grammar of tidymodels. Write a breeding scheme once, mark the choices you want to compare with tune(), and let tidyagsim run every design on the same replicate seeds, summarize the results with Monte Carlo standard errors, and help you pick. No nested loops, no hand-built results tables.

library(tidyagsim)

# A soybean-style line pipeline on AlphaSimR: how should 480 AYT plots be split?
pipeline <- line_pipeline(n_ayt = tune(), ayt_locations = tune(), ayt_reps = tune())

designs <- expand.grid(ayt_locations = c(1, 2, 4, 8), ayt_reps = c(1, 2))
designs$n_ayt <- 480 / (designs$ayt_locations * designs$ayt_reps)

res <- tune_grid(
  pipeline,
  resamples = sim_replicates(20, scenarios = sim_scenarios(gxe_var = c(0.2, 1))),
  grid = designs
)

collect_metrics(res)                          # tidy means and Monte Carlo SEs
show_best(res, metric = "gain_per_year")
autoplot(res)

Your own AlphaSimR scripts work the same way:

library(AlphaSimR)

recurrent <- alphasim_program(
  function(founders, SP, n_select, cycles) {
    tracker <- asr_tracker(founders)
    pop <- founders
    for (cycle in seq_len(cycles)) {
      pop <- randCross(selectInd(setPheno(pop), n_select), nCrosses = 200)
      tracker$record(pop, year = cycle, cost = 200 * 15)
    }
    asr_summary(tracker)
  },
  n_select = tune(), cycles = 10,
  params = list(n_select = sim_param(c(4, 60)))
)
tune_bayes(recurrent, sim_replicates(10), constraints = list(genetic_variance = 0.2))
tidymodels tidyagsim
parsnip model spec + tune() alphasim_program(), line_pipeline(), mapping_population(), sim_function() + tune()
dials extract_parameter_set_dials(), n_lines(), filial_generation(), …
rsample sim_replicates() (paired seeds), sim_scenarios()
yardstick metric_set() sim_metric_set()
tune_grid(), finetune::tune_race_anova(), tune_bayes() tune_grid(), tune_race(), tune_bayes() (with constraints)
collect_metrics(), show_best(), select_by_one_std_err() same names, plus pareto_front(), compare_designs()
workflowsets sim_set(), sim_map(), rank_results()

Simulators

  • alphasim_program(): any AlphaSimR breeding scheme, written as a function of the founders, SP and your design arguments. tidyagsim builds reproducible founders for each replicate (asr_founders()), and asr_tracker() / asr_summary() turn a run into gain, gain per year, gain per cost, remaining genetic variance and diversity.
  • line_pipeline(): a ready-made inbred line pipeline (crossing, single-seed descent, PYT, AYT, release and parent recycling) with G×E, costs and time.
  • mapping_population(): a fast simulator for QTL mapping populations (F2, recombinant inbred lines, BCsFt, nested association mapping, advanced-backcross NAM and 4- or 8-way MAGIC), with genome scans, permutation thresholds, costs and time to results.
  • backcross_program(): marker-assisted backcrossing of one or more target genes, with foreground, flanking-marker and background selection, simultaneous or parallel (pyramiding) strategies, and recurrent parent recovery, linkage drag, time and genotyping cost as metrics.
  • sim_function(): any R function of its arguments and a seed.
  • breeding_program(): a breedsim flowchart (from the desktop app), tuned by "stage.field" paths.

Learning tidyagsim

New to breeding simulation? The articles build up one idea at a time:

  1. Getting started: the grammar in five minutes.
  2. Why simulate?: checking a simulation against the breeder’s equation.
  3. How many replicates?: Monte Carlo error and paired seeds.
  4. Choosing a design: budgets, the one-standard-error rule and Pareto fronts.

Then the case studies: yield trial allocation, gene pyramiding and mapping population design.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jhgille2/tidyagsim")

On Windows this needs only R (4.1 or later); AlphaSimR installs from CRAN as a binary. For breeding_program() you also need Python with the breedsim package and the R package jsonlite. From PowerShell, in a clone of plant_breeding_simulator_flowchart:

py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e .

Then in R, point reticulate at that Python before loading tidyagsim:

Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = "C:/path/to/plant_breeding_simulator_flowchart/.venv/Scripts/python.exe")
Sys.setenv(BREEDSIM_RSCRIPT = "C:/Program Files/R/R-4.5.1/bin/Rscript.exe")  # if Rscript is not on PATH
